issues.title: Method brace on same line
issues.description: The rule requires opening braces to appear on a new line after method declarations, but this method has its opening brace on the same line as the declaration (K&R style).
issues.rule_name: Opening Braces Must Be on New Line (Allman Style)

issues.title: BackgroundQueueSize incorrectly rejects zero value despite 'non-negative' contract
issues.description: The BackgroundQueueSize property validation was changed to reject values less than or equal to zero, but the error message states 'must be non-negative' which includes zero. According to the XML documentation, null represents no limit. While zero is semantically different from null, the validation is now inconsistent with the documented contract that explicitly states 'non-negative' (which mathematically includes zero). This prevents callers from setting a zero queue size if that was their intent, even though zero is a valid non-negative integer. The validation logic contradicts the error message, creating a confusing API contract.

issues.title: RetainedFileCountLimit allows zero value violating positive-only constraint
issues.description: The RetainedFileCountLimit property validation was changed from rejecting values <= 0 to only rejecting values < 0, which now allows zero as a valid value. However, both the XML documentation and the error message explicitly state that this must be a 'positive' value, and zero is not positive. The remarks indicate this controls maximum retained file count - a value of zero would mean no log files are retained, which could lead to complete log loss. This violates the documented API contract and creates a dangerous configuration scenario where all logs could be immediately discarded.

issues.title: Premature null assignment in TryGetValidatableTypeInfo violates out parameter semantics
issues.description: The validatableTypeInfo out parameter is now being set to null at the beginning of the method before iterating through resolvers, rather than after the loop when no resolver was found. While this may appear equivalent, it violates proper out parameter semantics and the contract implied by [NotNullWhen(true)]. If a resolver incorrectly returns true while leaving the out parameter unassigned or null (a buggy resolver implementation), the early null assignment would mask this contract violation. Additionally, this creates unnecessary assignment overhead since the parameter will be overwritten by successful resolvers. The original pattern of assigning null only when no resolver succeeds is more semantically correct and provides better detection of misbehaving resolvers.

issues.title: Empty <returns> XML documentation on public method
issues.description: The public API method `AddAzureWebAppDiagnostics` includes a `<returns>` XML doc tag with no content. This results in incomplete XML documentation for a public API, violating the requirement that public APIs have complete XML documentation (including meaningful `<returns>` content when applicable).
issues.rule_name: Public APIs Must Have XML Documentation Comments

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #64092 - Doc updates

structured_output.summary:
This PR is labelled as a documentation update for APIs published under .NET monikers. Most of the diff is XML doc work: `<value>` and `<remarks>` sections, `<see langword>` in place of bare true/false/null, "Gets or sets" phrasing, and corrected defaults. The defaults I checked (10 MB file size, 2 retained files, 1000 queue size) match the code, and the rewrites read cleanly.

The PR also contains several non-documentation code changes that the description does not mention. `RetainedFileCountLimit` now accepts 0, which silently disables file pruning because `RollFiles` only prunes when the value is greater than 0. `BackgroundQueueSize` now rejects 0, but its error message still says "must be non-negative". A `ValidationOptions` method was reordered and has a brace-style change. None of these changes come with tests. One new remark also repeats an inaccurate claim: a full queue does not block, it drops messages.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The RetainedFileCountLimit guard change is a real regression hidden in a doc-only PR: a value of 0 that used to throw now silently keeps every log file. The rest of the doc work is fine once the undocumented code changes are reverted or split into a separate PR with tests. The inaccurate "starts blocking" remark should also be corrected.

architecture.overview:
The changed code is the Azure App Services logging stack plus the Validation options surface. `BatchingLoggerProvider` is the base class. It reads `BatchingLoggerOptions` once in its constructor, pushes messages into a bounded `BlockingCollection` with a non-blocking TryAdd, and a background task drains that queue in batches. `FileLoggerProvider` derives from it and uses `FileSizeLimit` and `RetainedFileCountLimit` to decide when to stop writing and when to delete old files.

The PR is mostly XML doc edits that do not change the architecture. The exceptions are three setter guards (`RetainedFileCountLimit`, `BackgroundQueueSize`) that move the accepted value range, and a reordering in `ValidationOptions.TryGetValidatableTypeInfo`. The reorder is behavior-neutral.
steps: Entry point: `AddAzureWebAppDiagnostics` registers `FileLoggerProvider` and `AzureFileLoggerOptions`, which inherit the `BatchingLoggerOptions` setters.
Options setters: `BackgroundQueueSize` and `RetainedFileCountLimit` now validate with `<= 0` and `< 0` respectively. Those guards decide which values reach the provider.
Provider constructor: `BatchingLoggerProvider` copies `BackgroundQueueSize` into `_queueSize`, and `Start` creates a bounded `BlockingCollection` from it.
Writing path: `FileLoggerProvider.RollFiles` only prunes old files when `_maxRetainedFiles > 0`, so 0 now means keep everything.
Validation: `ValidationOptions` resolves validation metadata by iterating resolvers. The PR moves the out-parameter null-reset to the top of the method, which does not change the outcome.

findings.title: RetainedFileCountLimit now accepts 0 and silently disables pruning
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Logging.AzureAppServices/src/AzureFileLoggerOptions.cs`, the `RetainedFileCountLimit` setter (around line 53) was changed from `value <= 0` to `value < 0`, which lets 0 through. `FileLoggerProvider.RollFiles` only prunes when the value is greater than 0, so 0 silently means unlimited retention, contradicting the "must be positive" message. Restore the `value <= 0` guard so the behavior matches the message and the original code. This is a doc-only PR, so keep the change minimal and do not alter the docs for this property beyond what is needed.

findings.title: BackgroundQueueSize rejects 0 but the error message says non-negative
findings.body:
`BackgroundQueueSize` now uses `value <= 0`, so 0 is rejected. The exception message still reads "must be non-negative", which is wrong for the new check and misleads anyone who hits it.

The old code accepted 0 at set time. The later `new BlockingCollection(..., 0)` call throws anyway, so the real behavior is that 0 fails. The change moves that failure earlier, which is reasonable, but the PR does not say so and the message is now incorrect.

::diff{file="src/Logging.AzureAppServices/src/BatchingLoggerOptions.cs" lines="44-52"}

Change the message to say "must be positive", matching the check and the "strictly positive" wording used elsewhere. Call the validation change out in the PR description, or move it to its own PR with a test.
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Logging.AzureAppServices/src/BatchingLoggerOptions.cs`, the `BackgroundQueueSize` setter (around lines 47-49) now rejects 0 (`value <= 0`), but the `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` message still says "must be non-negative". Update the message to "must be positive" so it matches the check. Do not change the guard itself unless you also update the docs and add a test. Mention in the PR description that this validation is tightened.

findings.title: New remark says the log sink blocks when the queue is full, but it drops messages
findings.body:
The new `<remarks>` text says: "After the maximum queue size is reached, the log event sink starts blocking." That is not what the code does. `BatchingLoggerProvider` enqueues with `_messageQueue.TryAdd(..., millisecondsTimeout: 0, ...)`, which returns immediately. When the queue is full the message is dropped and counted in `_messagesDropped`. The provider even logs "message(s) dropped because of queue size limit".

Since this PR is documentation work, the doc should be right. The base text had the same error, and this change carries it forward into a new section.

::diff{file="src/Logging.AzureAppServices/src/BatchingLoggerOptions.cs" lines="38-42"}

Replace the sentence with an accurate one, for example: "After the maximum queue size is reached, new log messages are dropped."
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Logging.AzureAppServices/src/BatchingLoggerOptions.cs`, the `<remarks>` on `BackgroundQueueSize` (around line 40) says the log event sink "starts blocking" when the queue is full. `BatchingLoggerProvider` uses `TryAdd` with a 0 ms timeout (around line 143) and drops messages, counting them in `_messagesDropped`. Rewrite the sentence to say new messages are dropped once the queue is full. Keep the rest of the doc wording.

findings.title: Unrelated reordering in ValidationOptions.TryGetValidatableTypeInfo
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Validation/src/ValidationOptions.cs`, `TryGetValidatableTypeInfo` (around lines 44-56) had `validatableTypeInfo = null;` moved from the end of the method to the top. Behavior is the same, but the move is unrelated to this doc-only PR. Restore the original position of the assignment, or leave the move and say so in the PR description.

findings.title: Brace placement breaks the file's style
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Validation/src/ValidationOptions.cs`, the `TryGetValidatableParameterInfo` signature (around line 66) has its opening brace on the same line as the parameter list. Move the `{` to its own line to match the rest of the file.

findings.title: Doc-only description hides several behavior changes and has no tests
findings.body:
The PR description says "Doc updates for APIs published under .NET monikers." Three of the changed files also change runtime validation: `RetainedFileCountLimit`, `BackgroundQueueSize`, and the `ValidationOptions` reorder. The description does not mention any of them, and no test in `src/Logging.AzureAppServices/test` covers the new boundary values (0 for either setter).

Reviewers who scan the PR as docs-only will miss these changes. Split them into their own PR with tests, or expand the description to list them and the reasoning.
findings.fixPrompt: This PR mixes behavior changes into a doc-only change. Either move the `RetainedFileCountLimit` and `BackgroundQueueSize` guard changes (in `AzureFileLoggerOptions.cs` and `BatchingLoggerOptions.cs`) and the `ValidationOptions.cs` reorder into a separate PR with unit tests for the boundary values (0 and negative), or update the PR description to list each behavior change and its rationale. Doc-only edits should stay in this PR.

findings.title: Doc comments are accurate and consistent across the PR
findings.body: The XML doc rewrites follow the conventions used elsewhere in the repo. They use `<see langword="true" />` and `<see langword="null" />`, separate defaults into `<value>` blocks, and move detailed behavior into `<remarks>`. I checked the stated defaults against the code: `FileSizeLimit` is 10 MB, `RetainedFileCountLimit` is 2, `BackgroundQueueSize` is 1000, and `ValidationOptions.MaxDepth` is 32. The `<code language="csharp">` change in `ValidateContext.cs` is also correct.

findings.title: Typo kept in Polly extensions doc
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/HttpClientFactory/Polly/src/DependencyInjection/PollyHttpClientBuilderExtensions.cs`, the class summary (around line 14) says "extensions methods". Change it to "extension methods".
